There he was shackled to another boy and forced into hard labour, and he was shot in the leg by Temple gunmen at the Port Kaituma airstrip while escaping in November 1978.

persons.outcome_quote: During the reunion, Tom learned that five people had died during the airstrip shooting. Congressman Leo Ryan, defector Patricia Parks, a photographer from the San Francisco Examiner, and two NBC news reporters were tragically lost during the shooting. Congressman Ryan remains the only US representative to be killed in the line of duty. 12 others were wounded, including Tom and his sister Tina, both of which had
persons.decisive_work_quote: I think it's important to highlight that without the push of Congressman Ryan and journalists like Tim Reiterman investigating Jonestown, the Boge family, as well as the other defector families may not have lived that day.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: The same day the family told Congressman Ryan they wanted to leave (18 November 1978), after roughly 13 years in the Temple; it was his first institutional contact.
persons.notes: Protection is partial: leaving with the congressional delegation got him out of Jonestown before the mass deaths, but he was shot at the airstrip while under the delegation's escort and spent three days wounded in the jungle. The perpetrator was not stopped by any institution; he died at Jonestown the same day. The decisive work is unclear because the host credits Ryan and journalists together; Ryan's visit was prompted by a defector's father, the Concerned Relatives Group and an Examiner article (s4-e5-close-the-door-or-die @ 7:15), and the family's own escape plan and approach to Ryan also mattered. Not coded as contacts: (a) at age 9 a maintenance worker 'called it in' and unnamed people picked him up, put him in a church overnight and sent him to his aunt (s4-e1-theres-no-comfort-to-run-to-season-four-escaping-jonestown @ 17:35); it is unclear who they were or whether the abuse was raised, and his mother took him back. (b) At the Jonestown nurses' station the leader's son and wife saw the shackle wounds and the shackles were removed '[perpetrator] said to take... the shackles off' (s4-e4-we-will-kill-you @ 16:31): this was the Temple's own infirmary under the perpetrator's authority, not an outside institution. Later unrelated harms (slugged by a stranger at 19, scammed at 22; s4-e6-learned-to-fight-back-in-my-dreams @ 20:06) are bare mentions with no story, so no separate records. Evidence: book excerpts (A Thousand Lives, Raven) and Tom's 2013 essay read on air; Jim corroborates.

persons.name: Jim
persons.harm: An adult member for 13 years, he was blackmailed with a coerced false confession to molesting his daughters. The Temple turned his wife against him, left him penniless and homeless, made him transport stolen food and then forced him, under threat of prosecution, into exile and labour in Guyana, where he was kept low, watched and publicly berated.

contacts.what_was_asked: Nothing; police stopped the truck carrying stolen government food that the Temple had him drive.
contacts.what_institution_did: Held him personally responsible for the stolen food. The Temple then used the threat of prosecution, made credible because the district attorney and some deputies were Temple members, to force him to go to Guyana.
contacts.quote: And I was driving a truck loaded with this food and all to take it to this place where we was going to hide it. And the county woman somewhere pulled us over. And I had to accept that it was my job. Right. You know, it was my thing, separate from the group. Right. You could be held responsible. I was held responsible.
contacts.what_happened_next: Given the choice of prosecution or going to Guyana, he went to build Jonestown.
contacts.notes: The police learned of the incident, not of the coercion behind it; it is included because the forced crime was part of the abuse tactic the season describes ('putting them in illegal situations, forcing members to take the blame, then using the incident as blackmail', s4-e1-theres-no-comfort-to-run-to-season-four-escaping-jonestown @ 26:56). Whether he was ever charged is not stated. The DA's membership is Tom's account. 'county woman' is probably a transcription of 'county [man/sheriff]'; it is left as transcribed.

persons.harm: Jim and Edith's daughter, brought to Jonestown in 1977. She stayed when the family left because her husband stayed and the leader 'had really captured her', and she died in the mass killing at Jonestown on 18 November 1978.

persons.harm: Tom's mother and Jim's wife, a devoted Temple member. The leader directed her actions, including against her husband, and used her relationship with another member to control him. She lived under Jonestown's conditions from 1977 until she and her partner secretly asked the visiting party for help leaving.

persons.perpetrator_role: the People's Temple leader and Temple leadership

quotes.quote: So we started walking again and it sure as hell, they caught us from both sides and took us back.
He often spoke of how much he wanted to go back home to his mothers, but his dad wouldn't let him.

persons.outcome_quote: And so they decided that they were going to chain and shackle us together and make us work 18 hours a day hard labor. So this is active what they did. We went out to the warehouse and they had made these shackles with chains to put between us and they welded them on our legs
persons.notes: 'other' reason: the Temple recaptured the boys before they could reach the military post at Matthews Ridge and the US consulate they were heading for (s4-e4-we-will-kill-you @ 11:29). His father kept him from his mother. After the first escape (he took a Greyhound ticket bought with money skimmed from collection cans) the season does not say how he came back; 'a couple of years later, they sent him' to Jonestown (s4-e4-we-will-kill-you @ 9:24). The shackles were removed at the Temple's own nurses' station on the leader's order (not an outside institution). His fate after the shackling is not stated; whether he survived 18 November 1978 is unknown, so deceased is false (unknown). His story rests on Tom's account and Tom's 2013 essay read on air.

persons.name: Bob Houston
persons.harm: A long-time railroad worker and principal Temple member who defected and was found crushed between train cars in a San Francisco train yard in 1976. The survivors believe the Temple killed him as a warning to defectors.
persons.perpetrator_role: alleged: the People's Temple (the survivors believe the leader's people killed him); not established in the season

contacts.institution: US Congress: California Congressman Leo Ryan
contacts.what_was_asked: His father asked his friend the congressman to help look into the suspicious death and to help reconnect with his granddaughters, who were still being raised in the church.
contacts.what_institution_did: Ryan agreed to help and, also prompted by an Examiner article and the Concerned Relatives Group, went to Jonestown with journalists and relatives.
contacts.quote: Congressman Leo generously agreed to do his best to help his friend find answers. After reading an article on allegations against the People's Temple in the San Francisco Examiner, Congressman Ryan declared his intention to visit Jonestown. His decision was also influenced by the Concerned Relatives Group, which consisted of church members worried family members.
contacts.what_happened_next: Ryan visited Jonestown and was killed at the airstrip on 18 November 1978; the season reports no finding on Bob's death.
contacts.notes: Basis is host narration (apparently drawn from Raven). His father also worked with journalist Tim Reiterman at the AP, which is how Reiterman learned of the alleged killings of defectors (s4-e5-close-the-door-or-die @ 6:14); that was journalism, not an institution.

persons.outcome_quote: Bob Houston, he was in San Francisco, there somewhere, but he was killed in the train yards. He said it was a suicide, but we know it wasn't.
persons.notes: Who said 'it was a suicide' is ambiguous: it could be the leader or an official finding, and it is not coded as a contact. The cause of death is contested in the season (the host calls it a 'suspect train yard incident'). He died, so the outcome is not_protected. Tom and Jim both spoke about him.

So the next thing Ryan knew is he had a group on his hands that wanted to leave. Everything wasn't rosy and paradise. And that was the first news he got of it that away because until then it had been playing the role. So he said, okay, you know, as well, you guys go get on the truck and, you know, we're gonna start heading out to the airport.
contacts.what_happened_next: At the airstrip, Temple gunmen attacked the planes; Ryan and four others were killed and others wounded.
contacts.notes: The Parks family went first: 'we heard that the the parks family had gone to Ryan and told them they wanted to leave' (s4-e5-close-the-door-or-die @ 12:29).

persons.outcome_quote: And at that point, Patti Parks, who was sitting right in front of me in the airplane, I'm sitting right across from the door. She gets the back of her head shot off.
persons.notes: Killed while under the delegation's escort, so not protected. Host narration names her as 'defector Patricia Parks' among the dead (s4-e6-learned-to-fight-back-in-my-dreams @ 2:03).

coder_notes: Season 4 (Escaping Jonestown, E1-E8) tells the Bogue family's People's Temple story. E8 is a COVID-19 mental-health interview with no harm stories. The perpetrator's name is replaced with [perpetrator] throughout, and so are the names of the airstrip gunman and other Temple agents inside quotations. The central institutional contact for most people is Congressman Leo Ryan's delegation (coded institution_type 'other': US Congress). Its visit was prompted by a defector's father, the Concerned Relatives Group and press reports. The perpetrator died at Jonestown, and the season reports no prosecution of anyone. Key judgment calls: (1) the Temple's own nurses' station and the leader's family are not treated as outside institutions; (2) a sheriff's deputy serving eviction and separation papers on Jim at the leader's instigation is not coded as a contact because the harm was not raised (see Jim's notes); (3) the police stop where Jim was 'held responsible' for the stolen food the Temple made him move is coded as a contact; (4) the FBI interviews are coded did_nothing_or_delayed under the 'report taken, no further step shown' rule; (5) protection is coded partly_protected for the survivors who got out, because the escape under the delegation's escort ended in the airstrip shooting. The host's dedication to her murdered brother (E4) is outside the season's story and is not recorded. All three chunk files were read in full. A bare mention of a young woman said to stay with the leader (E4 @ 21:48) is left out of others_mentioned because the only quotable passage names her and it is unclear whether the show presents her as harmed.
